phases: 1-6 (scoped by the owner to the capture path: spec §6.2, D86, D115, D116)
headline: The masking net works on every ordinary shape: amounts kept, dedupe key from the masked text, no code anywhere in the outbox file, and the screen and simulator show it as patterns.md says. Two gaps let a code through unmasked. The mask misses numbers the filter itself reads as codes (thin, en or ideographic space, tab, circled digits). And OTP wording with no listed word ('nombor pengesahan', 'sahkan', 'verify') is stored raw.

suites.QA core probes: 217 tests, 193 pass, 24 red (23 are run 5's findings; Probe4.r4_merchant_tac_store_no is run 4's deliberate red)
suites.e2e: QA run 5: 5/5 pass; the branch's capture.spec.ts 9/9 on QA's build

findings.title: The mask misses codes the filter itself reads as codes, so they're stored raw and unmarked
findings.detail: `OtpMask.RUN` joins digits only across ` `, U+00A0, U+2007, U+202F, `.`, `,`, `/`, `-`, U+2010-2013 and a few invisible characters, and counts digits with `Character.isDigit(char)`. The filter (`OtpFilter.sentences`) reads text after NFKC, so a thin space (U+2009), en space (U+2002), ideographic space (U+3000) or tab becomes a space, and circled or math-bold digits become digits. The filter drops `Your TAC is 482\u2009913.` as an OTP. But in the shape it keeps (the OTP word only in advice), the mask sees two 3-digit runs, masks nothing, and `mask()` returns null. So the event is stored with the code readable and `maybe_otp = 0`. D116's purpose, 'so no possible code is ever stored', fails for numbers the native code itself calls codes. Rarer groupings fail the same way (middle dot, em dash, minus sign, underscore, `(482) 913`). The filter doesn't read those as codes either. Math-bold digits are surrogate pairs, so `Character.isDigit(char)` is false on each half.

findings.title: An OTP worded without a listed word is stored raw: the net's trigger is the same kind of word list that runs 1-4 kept beating
findings.detail: The mask fires only on the filter's strong and weak words plus a few plurals and `token`. A chosen bank's OTP that says 'pengesahan', 'sahkan', 'log masuk', 'verify' or 'verification number' has none of them. The filter keeps it, and the mask leaves it alone, so the code is stored as posted, with `maybe_otp = 0`. That follows D116's letter ('has an OTP word') but not its purpose, or CLAUDE.md's non-negotiable. 'Masukkan 482913 untuk sahkan transaksi' and 'Nombor pengesahan anda' are plausible Malay wordings. A false mask costs only digits, which the drafter (B10) gets back by judging the event. So the mask's trigger can afford to be far broader than the filter's: verification and login words in English and Malay, or (for the owner) any kept notification with a 6-digit run outside an amount. Owner question: how wide the mask's trigger should be.

findings.title: About 2 KB of digit-heavy text overflows the mask's regex stack, uncaught on the capture thread
findings.detail: On the JVM with a 1 MB thread stack (what Android gives a plain Java thread), `OtpMask.maskDigits` throws `java.lang.StackOverflowError` from `java.util.regex` (`Pattern$Loop`/`GroupHead` recursion) on a run of about 2,030 digits, 1,025 spaced single digits, 284 `482 913 ` groups or 608 `12, ` pairs. Each is about 2 KB, under the 5,120 characters a notification field keeps. It needs an OTP word in the text too. `Capture.store` runs `gate.decide` on the `sen-capture` executor with no catch. On Android an uncaught Throwable on any thread kills the process. When the listener reconnects it replays the notification still showing, so the crash would repeat until it's dismissed. **Not verified on Android:** ART's `java.util.regex` is backed by ICU, which backtracks on a heap stack rather than the thread's, so the device may not overflow at all. Unlikely from a real bank, but any app chosen through *More* controls its own text. Suggested: cap the text the mask and filter read, catch Throwable around `decide` (dropping, and logging the drop, on error), and add an emulator test with a 5,000-character digit run.

findings.title: The mask joins unrelated numbers and can eat a whole-ringgit amount, changing raw text beyond a run of four digits
findings.detail: A run may span up to three separator characters, including `, ` and `. `. So `No. 123, 9:47 PM` counts 1-2-3-9 as one four-digit run and is stored as `No. •••, •:47 PM`: neither number is a run of four. The currency check is `(rm|myr|usd|sgd|\$)\s?$`, where Java's `\s` excludes U+00A0 and allows one space. So `RM\u00A02500`, `RM  2500` and `RM\u00A02,500` lose the amount (`RM\u00A0••••`), though §6.2 says amounts are left. Decimal amounts are safe. Harm: B09/B10 can't read such a payment's amount from the stored text.

findings.title: OtpMaskTest's invisible-character case has no teeth
findings.detail: The one zero-width case in `codes in every shape are masked` is `48\u200B2910`, split 2+4. The 4-digit half is masked whether or not the mask understands invisible characters, and `assertNoCode` passes with `48` left. Taking the invisible-character class out of `OtpMask.RUN` (probe 6) leaves all 39 core tests green. QA's `Probe5.ac52_zero_width` (`48\u200B29\u200B13`) goes red under the same probe. Suggested: split 3+3 or 2+2+2.

findings.title: The simulator's maybe-OTP is hand-masked text: a browser walk shows the display, never the mask
findings.detail: `sim.maybeOtp()` stores a fixed, already-masked string with `maybeOtp: true`, and `post()` cycles four fixed samples. No input reaches a mask in the browser, so FLOW-15 to FLOW-20 prove the row, the line and the replay, not the masking. The one sample matches the core exactly (`Probe5.ac59s_sim_sample_matches_core`). Fine as a simulator, as long as nobody reads a browser walk as evidence of masking.

findings.title: The emulator test's 'the code is nowhere in the outbox' reads only events' three text fields
findings.detail: `CaptureListenerTest.a_notification_that_might_hold_a_code_is_stored_masked_and_marked` checks `title`, `text` and `bigText` of `events(500)`. The heartbeat log and `channel_drops` have no text columns, so the claim holds by the schema, and QA's SQLite check found neither code nor raw-text key anywhere in the file. The test's comment claims more than it checks.

findings.title: Chinese OTPs and a spelled-out 'T A C' are stored raw
findings.detail: `您的验证码是482913` and `… Never share your T A C.` are kept with the code readable. The filter is specified for English and Malay (brief, §6.2), so this is outside the spec as written. Listed because Malaysian apps do post Chinese, and D116 is meant to catch what the lists miss.
